Sand seeps. Rock cracks. Both steal your fluid.
In sand, your mud pushes through millions of tiny pores. The wall softens and starts closing in.

In fractured rock, the losses come fast. Open cracks swallow fluid before you can top the tank.

Different ground, same fix. Build a thin, tough filter cake on the bore wall before the ground takes control.

That's the job Filter Low does. Seals the wall and keeps the fluid on your side of it.
Sand or rock, where do you lose the most fluid?

Filter Low is in six of our fluid programs.
HDD in sand, waterwell in reactive clay, bored piling before a concrete pour. Every one needs a sealed bore wall, and every one runs Filter Low.

It's a PAC polymer that seals the wall without thickening your mud. The pump runs easy, the fluid stays thin, and the bore holds.

Works in bentonite systems and polymer systems. Rated to 149 degrees for geothermal work.

For tougher ground or bigger losses, give one of our team a call. We'll dial in the right dose for the job.
Which discipline gives you the worst fluid loss?
